name: What does a commercial project manager do on a Los Angeles tenant improvement project?

mainEntity.name: What does a commercial project manager actually handle on a tenant improvement project in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What does a commercial project manager actually handle on a tenant improvement project in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A commercial project manager on a tenant improvement project is responsible for turning the design and budget into a buildable plan. That usually includes scope review, schedule creation, permit coordination, bid leveling, subcontractor selection, procurement tracking, change-order control, site meetings, inspections, and punch-list completion. In active Los Angeles properties, the role also includes coordinating with tenants, landlords, property managers, and building operations so construction does not disrupt normal business more than necessary. The best project managers keep decisions moving, document everything, and flag issues early before they become delays or cost overruns. For owners, the value is not just supervision, but risk control and accountability across the entire project. If a project is in a multi-tenant building or has strict operating hours, the project manager also has to plan phasing, access, noise control, and shutdown windows carefully.
acceptedAnswer.description: A commercial project manager coordinates scope, budget, schedule, permits, subcontractors, inspections, and client communication from preconstruction through closeout. On tenant improvements, they also manage phasing so the business can keep operating, reduce downtime, and keep the work aligned with lease, building, and landlord requirements.
